text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistanis go to the polls on Monday to elect 217 members for the National Assembly (lower house) and 460 for the four provincial assemblies.
- Foreign observers belonging to South Asian, Commonwealth and European countries will monitor Monday's general elections.

- Pakistan People's Party (PPP), Pakistan Muslim League and Tehrik-i-Insaaf (Justice Movement) leaders wrapped up their election campaigns in Lahore by addressing rallies and predicting victory for their respective parties.
- Prices of natural gas, electricity and petroleum products will be increased by another 25 percent over the next five months, a top official said in an interview.
- President Farooq Leghari said that all arrangements for holding free, fair and transparent elections on February 3 had been completed by the Election Commission.
- Election results for 115 National Assembly and 240 provincial assmbly seats in Punjab province are going to spring many surprises, political observers say.

- A Mohajir National Movement (MQM) motorcade was attacked with rotten eggs, potatoes and bricks when it entered Landhi, Malir and Shah Faisal Colony in Karachi's eastern district controlled by the rival Haqqiqi faction of the party.
- Pakistan's largest air separation and hydrogen plant is being set up at Port Qasim to meet local industry demand.

- Foreign direct investment in Pakistan is expected to soar to $16.738 billion during the 9th five-year plan to be launched next year owing to major structural changes in the rules governing foreign capital.
- The caretaker government has decided to reduce the market share of Habib Bank Limited by dividing it into two or more banks.
- Maleeha Lodhi has relinquished charge as Pakistan's ambassador in Washington on completion of her tenure.
- A survery conducted by the English-language daily The News said Nawaz Sharif would get a clear majority in the elections.
- State (central) Bank Governor Muhammad Yaqub said the forward cover facility on foreign currency deposits may be withdrawn.
